subject: What happens during a home consultation
hook: One badly placed socket can push a whole media unit off-centre. That is why we note them first.
ig:
One badly placed socket can push a whole media unit off-centre. That is why we note them first.

When we come out for a design consultation, a surprising amount of time goes on the boring bits:

• Sockets and switches: where they sit decides where a TV unit, desk or worktop appliance can go, and whether a drawer will clash with a plug.
• Radiators: fitted furniture in front of one traps heat, so the layout has to leave it room or plan around it.
• Skirting height: it decides whether units are scribed over it or the skirting is cut back.
• Window boards and reveals: they set how close a tall unit can sit.

Spotting these at the start means fewer compromises later, and an itemised quote that reflects the real room rather than a perfect box.

Which of these is the awkward one in your room? Tell us below and we will say how we would handle it.
fb:
Here is something people do not expect from a design consultation: we spend a good while looking at your sockets.

It sounds dull, but a socket in the wrong place can push a media unit off-centre, stop a drawer opening, or leave a plug stuck behind a cupboard. Radiators, skirting boards and window reveals are the same story. Noting them at the first visit means the design works around your actual room, not an ideal one.

If there is a socket, radiator or awkward corner holding your plans back, tell us about it in the comments, or see what we make here:
